aiEstimate.basis: Strict proof-completion estimate: 0%. Exact identities, necessary orbit restrictions, and residue-sensitive descent tests with local carry thresholds are recorded, but no argument proves descent for every odd starting value. These local conditions do not quantify full theorem completion.

focus.status: Pure math · global descent theorem open
focus.title: Control residue carries across block transitions
focus.summary: Each block with C>0 contracts exactly when its residue carry Q_k reaches an explicit threshold. The unresolved step is to prove that the coupled transition sequence crosses enough thresholds for every starting orbit.
focus.next: Derive a recurrence or global inequality controlling the frequency of Q_k≥Q_k^{min}, including the C≤0 expansion blocks.

accomplishments.title: Proof target made precise
accomplishments.detail: Reduce the full conjecture to showing that every odd n > 1 has a smaller odd iterate under the Syracuse map.

accomplishments.title: Exact cumulative-valuation criterion derived
accomplishments.detail: For an odd Syracuse orbit, 2^A_j S^j(n) = 3^j n + c_j and descent is equivalent to (2^A_j − 3^j)n > c_j.

accomplishments.title: Exact run length of valuation-one steps proved
accomplishments.detail: Starting from odd n, exactly v2(n+1)−1 consecutive Syracuse steps have valuation 1; the following step has valuation at least 2. This proves larger valuations recur, but not often enough yet to force descent.

accomplishments.title: Exact return-block descent criterion derived
accomplishments.detail: For a valuation-a≥2 step followed by its forced run of t−1 valuation-one steps, the endpoint satisfies 3(z−x)=2^a−2−u(2^{a+t}−2·3^t). This gives an exact local test, while allowing some blocks to grow.

accomplishments.title: Modulo-three restriction on return blocks proved
accomplishments.detail: The block integrality equation forces 3|u for odd a, and u≡(−1)^{t+1} mod 3 for even a. This raises the minimum possible u and sharpens sufficient local descent conditions.

accomplishments.title: Exact transition law between return blocks derived
accomplishments.detail: Successive blocks satisfy a_{k+1}−1=v2(3^{t_k}u_k−1), equivalently 3^{t_k}u_k−1=2^{a_{k+1}−1}(2^{t_{k+1}}u_{k+1}−1). The long-run consequence is still open.

accomplishments.title: Critical mean for local block descent proved
accomplishments.detail: If a block's mean valuation (a+t−1)/t is at most log₂3, its endpoint is strictly larger than its start. Therefore a contracting block must exceed this mean, but that condition alone is not sufficient.

accomplishments.title: Guaranteed-descent mean threshold derived
accomplishments.detail: A block is guaranteed to contract when q=(a+t−1)/t exceeds λ_t=1+(1/t)log₂((3^t−1)/(2^t−1))=log₂3+η_t, with η_t positive and tending to zero. The coarse test is inconclusive in the band between thresholds.

accomplishments.title: Explicit bound on the threshold gap derived
accomplishments.detail: Writing η_t=(1/t)log₂(1+δ_t), where δ_t=(2^{-t}−3^{-t})/(1−2^{-t}), gives 0<η_t<2^{1−t}/(t ln 2). The local uncertainty shrinks exponentially with block length.

accomplishments.title: Exact logarithmic block-drift identity derived
accomplishments.detail: The endpoint ratio telescopes to Σ(a_k−1)=j log₂(3/2)+Σε_k−log₂((x_{m+1}+1)/(n+1)), where each ε_k is positive and bounded by −log₂(1−2^{-t_k}). This gives a block-length-sensitive necessary cap, not a proof of descent.

accomplishments.title: Exact state-dependent block contraction test derived
accomplishments.detail: A block contracts exactly when q_k exceeds log₂3 plus ε_k/t_k, where ε_k=log₂(1+(2^{a_k}−2)/(3(x_k+1))). Summed block drift below −r log₂(3/2) places a block-boundary iterate below the original n.

accomplishments.title: Cumulative block-excess constraint derived
accomplishments.detail: Across m complete blocks, A_j−j=Σ(a_k−1). If the orbit never drops below n, this excess must be at most j log₂((3+1/n)/2) at each block boundary. Proving a contradictory lower bound remains open.

accomplishments.title: Monotone block threshold proved
accomplishments.detail: The universal sufficient mean λ_t=log₂3+η_t decreases strictly to log₂3. Thus any fixed margin above log₂3 guarantees contraction for sufficiently long blocks; whether every orbit attains the needed means remains open.

accomplishments.title: Mean tests isolate one possible valuation gap
accomplishments.detail: For fixed block length t, a≤floor(t log₂(3/2))+1 forces expansion, while a≥floor(t log₂(3/2))+3 guarantees contraction. At most one integer a remains for the exact u-dependent test; this is local and does not control orbit-wide drift.

accomplishments.title: The possible valuation gap reduced to an integer test
accomplishments.detail: For the sole candidate a=floor(t log₂(3/2))+2, universal contraction is immediate if 1−{t log₂(3/2)}>log₂R_t. Otherwise the exact block test is uD>2^{h+1}−1, where h=floor(t log₂(3/2)) and D=2^{h+t+1}−3^t>0. This remains a local criterion.

accomplishments.title: An expanding gap block forces the next valuation down
accomplishments.detail: For a=h+2 and uD≤2^{h+1}−1, the transition law gives a_next−1=v₂(Du+1). Strict expansion implies a_next≤a−1; equality in the block test is a periodic return. This is a local transition constraint, not a global descent proof.

accomplishments.title: Expanding gap blocks split into two exact transitions
accomplishments.detail: For a strict expansion, write r=Du+1=2^b s with s odd and ℓ=t+h+1−b. If s>1, then a_next+t_next≤a_k−1; if s=1, then t_next=ℓ≥t+1 and u_next=u. This is an exact local dichotomy, not a global descent proof.

accomplishments.title: The long-run branch forces a second expansion
accomplishments.detail: In the s=1 branch after a strict gap-block expansion, t_next≥t+1, u_next=u, and q_next=1+b/t_next<log₂3. The critical mean test therefore forces the next block to expand too. This is still only a local sequence constraint.

accomplishments.title: Exceptional expansion chains have a square-root bound
accomplishments.detail: For a chain of L consecutive strict expansions at the possible mean-test gap, each link must have s>1, so t decreases and H=a+t drops by at least t+1. Since H≥3, (L+1)(L+2)≤2H_start; hence L≤floor((sqrt(8H_start+1)−3)/2). This excludes only an infinite consecutive run of this expansion type.

accomplishments.title: Exceptional expansion chains have a uniform growth cap
accomplishments.detail: At the gap, d_i=ε_i−(1−f_i), so a strict expansion has 0<d_i<β_{t_i}. Since the t_i in a chain are distinct, the total logarithmic growth is below Σ_{t≥1}β_t≤2/ln 2. Thus (x_end+1)/(x_start+1)<e², independent of the starting value.

accomplishments.title: Exceptional expansion chains grow by less than 32/9
accomplishments.detail: Each strict exceptional expansion has 0<d_i<β_{t_i}; the t_i in a chain are distinct. The product P=∏_{t≥1}(1−2^{-t}) is at least 9/32, so Σd_i≤−log₂P≤log₂(32/9). Telescoping gives (x_end+1)/(x_start+1)<32/9, uniformly in the starting value.

If S(x)=y and S(y)=x for positive odd x,y, exact elimination gives (2^(a+b)−9)x=2^a+3 and (2^(a+b)−9)y=2^b+3. The valuation cases force x=y=1. This excludes only periods 1 and 2, not longer cycles or divergent orbits.
accomplishments.title: Nontrivial odd-only cycles of period at most two excluded
Odd-only cycles of period at most four excluded
accomplishments.detail: Multiplying cycle step ratios gives 3^m<2^A<(10/3)^m for any nontrivial m-cycle. This excludes m=1,2,4; for m=3 it forces A=5, and the exact cycle equation modulo 5 rules out every positive valuation triple. Longer cycles and nonperiodic orbits remain open.

If no odd iterate falls below n, then Σ(a_i−1)≤j c_n, where c_n=log₂((3+1/n)/2). Therefore the count of a_i≥s is at most floor(j c_n/(s−1)), valuation-one steps have lower density at least log₂(6/5), and the mean return-block length has lower limit at least 1/c_n. These necessary conditions do not yet contradict the transition law.
accomplishments.title: Necessary valuation frequencies for a descent failure derived
Transition telescope matched to next-block drift correction
accomplishments.detail: The logarithmic transition correction δ_k equals ε_{k+1} exactly, using x_{k+1}+1=2·3^{t_k−1}u_k. This telescopes the known block-drift correction in (t,u) coordinates and gives a necessary endpoint-parameter inequality under non-descent. It supplies no independent bound or contradiction.

Modulo 3^{t_k}, the transition gives u_{k+1}≡2^{−(b_k+t_{k+1})}(2^{b_k}−1), with b_k=a_{k+1}−1. LTE yields min(v₃(u_{k+1}),t_k)=min(t_k,1+v₃(b_k)) for even b_k and 0 for odd b_k. This strengthens the inherited lower bound on u for odd next valuations and gives a sharper local contraction test, but not an orbit-wide descent proof.
accomplishments.title: Higher 3-adic divisibility across block transitions derived
Transition-aware finite-prefix descent certificate sharpened
accomplishments.detail: Define U_k from the parity/modulo-3 block condition and, for odd a_k after the first block, the inherited bound 3^{min(t_{k−1},1+v₃(a_k−1))}. Then ε_k<−log₂(1−1/(2^{t_k}U_k)). If the sum of t_k(log₂3−q_k)−log₂(1−1/(2^{t_k}U_k)) over a prefix is below −r log₂(3/2), its endpoint is below n. This sharpens a sufficient certificate but does not prove every orbit meets it.

The transition determines u_k modulo M_k=3^{t_{k−1}}. Its least positive odd representative U_k* is obtained from the residue R_k by choosing R_k if odd and R_k+M_k if even, so u_k≥U_k*. This replaces a valuation-only lower bound in ε_k<−log₂(1−1/(2^{t_k}U_k*)) and sharpens the finite-prefix descent test. For 9→17 it recovers u_2≥7 exactly. Orbit-wide prefix existence remains open.
accomplishments.title: Full 3-adic residues sharpen the block descent certificate

accomplishments.detail: Writing u_{k+1}=U_{k+1}*+2·3^{t_k}Q_k converts the block endpoint difference to B_{k+1}−C_{k+1}U_{k+1}*−2·3^{t_k}C_{k+1}Q_k. For C≤0 the block expands; for C>0 it contracts exactly when Q_k≥max(0,floor((B−CU*)/(2·3^{t_k}C))+1). This gives a local exact threshold; orbit-wide control of the carries remains open.
accomplishments.title: Exact carry threshold for block contraction derived

notes.text: Using the exact 3-adic residue lift, write u_{k+1}=U_{k+1}*+2·3^{t_k}Q_k. The next block contracts exactly above an explicit integer threshold in Q_k when C_{k+1}>0; if C≤0 it expands. Significance: 17/100 — an exact local dichotomy, with carry-frequency control still open.
notes.speaker: Codex · residue-carry threshold

notes.text: The transition fixes u_k modulo 3^{t_{k−1}}. Because u_k is positive odd and the modulus is odd, its least possible value is R_k when the least residue is odd, or R_k+3^{t_{k−1}} when it is even. This yields a stronger ε_k bound and sharpens the prefix descent certificate; for 9→17 it recovers u_2=7. Significance: 19/100 — a stronger local certificate, with orbit-wide coverage still open.
notes.speaker: Codex · exact residue lift

notes.text: Using inherited 3-adic divisibility, each block has u_k≥U_k and hence ε_k<Γ_k=−log₂(1−1/(2^{t_k}U_k)). Therefore any prefix with Σ[t_k(log₂3−q_k)+Γ_k]<−r log₂(3/2) certifies descent. Significance: 18/100 — a stronger finite-prefix certificate; existence of such a prefix on every orbit remains open.
notes.speaker: Codex · sharpened descent test

notes.text: New exact local constraint: reducing 2^{b_k+t_{k+1}}u_{k+1}=3^{t_k}u_k+2^{b_k}−1 modulo 3^{t_k} fixes u_{k+1} mod 3^{t_k}. LTE gives v₃(u_{k+1})≥min(t_k,1+v₃(b_k)) when b_k=a_{k+1}−1 is even. This improves a local contraction test, while orbit-wide control remains open. Significance: 16/100.
notes.speaker: Codex · 3-adic transition update
Codex · identity audit
notes.text: Formula audit: the positive transition correction δ_k is exactly the existing next-block drift correction ε_{k+1}. The telescope is a transition-coordinate re-expression of the known block drift, not an independent estimate. The remaining task is to bound cumulative drift or terminal parameters independently. Significance: 8/100.

Taking logarithms in the exact block transition gives a telescoping identity with strictly positive correction δ_k. Combined with the no-descent valuation cap, it yields a necessary inequality: terminal (1+c_n)t+log₂u must absorb the accumulated corrections beyond allowance (c_n−log₂(3/2))Σt. Significance: 16/100 — a sharper structural relation, but no contradiction yet.
notes.speaker: Codex · transition potential
Codex · orbit-frequency bound
notes.text: For a hypothetical descent failure from odd n>1, the exact cumulative-valuation cap implies N_s(j)≤floor(j c_n/(s−1)), where c_n=log₂((3+1/n)/2) and N_s counts valuations a_i≥s. Thus valuation-one steps have lower density at least log₂(6/5), and complete return blocks have mean length at least 1/c_n in the limit. Significance: 18/100 — a structural restriction on any counterexample, but not yet a contradiction.

notes.speaker: Codex · cycle bound
notes.text: Exact cycle result: for any nontrivial odd-only cycle of period m, multiplying the step ratios yields 3^m<2^A<(10/3)^m. This rules out periods 1, 2, and 4 directly; period 3 forces A=5 and is excluded by its exact equation modulo 5. Significance: 14/100 — a small-cycle exclusion only; longer cycles and nonperiodic orbits remain open.

Pure-algebra side result: the odd-only Syracuse map has no nontrivial orbit whose period divides 2. Eliminating the two step equations forces x=y=1. Significance: 12/100; it closes only the smallest cycle cases and does not prove descent or rule out longer cycles.
notes.speaker: Codex · cycle lemma
Project direction
notes.text: The project is pivoting from the UCT conjecture to Collatz. The plan is to move slowly, use small checkable tasks, and build a map toward a full proof.

notes.speaker: Codex · research update
notes.text: Earlier, we proved a local descent certificate for n ≡ 2587 (mod 4096). It remains a partial result; the current direction studies general valuation identities.

notes.speaker: Codex · theory update
notes.text: We grouped the orbit into blocks: each has length t and valuation sum a+t−1, so A_j−j=Σ(a_k−1). A non-descending orbit must keep this excess below j log₂((3+1/n)/2) at block boundaries. The missing step is a dynamics-based lower bound; blocks can expand, as 9→7→11→17 shows.

notes.speaker: Codex · algebra update
notes.text: Using 3x=2^{a+t}u−2^a−1, integrality forces u to be divisible by 3 when a is odd, and fixes u modulo 3 when a is even. This sharpens which return blocks can contract; the global cumulative bound is still open.

notes.speaker: Codex · dynamics update
notes.text: A block contracts exactly when q_k>log₂3+ε_k/t_k. Summed block drifts below −r log₂(3/2) guarantee a return value below n. The open task is an orbit-wide inequality forcing such descent for every odd start.

notes.speaker: Project direction
notes.text: The proof path is centered on exact Syracuse identities, valuation constraints, and inequalities that apply to every odd starting value. Finite orbit checks and growing residue tables are kept outside the proof strategy.

notes.speaker: Codex · threshold update
notes.text: The universal block threshold λ_t decreases strictly to log₂3. Any fixed positive margin above log₂3 therefore guarantees contraction for sufficiently long blocks. Proving that the coupled parameters of every orbit supply this margin remains open.

notes.speaker: Codex · local criterion update
notes.text: For each fixed block length t, the mean tests classify every valuation a except possibly one integer level: lower a forces expansion, higher a guarantees contraction, and the single possible gap is resolved by the exact u-dependent formula. This narrows a local criterion only; the global orbit problem remains open.

notes.speaker: Codex · arithmetic refinement
notes.text: The one possible valuation gap now has an exact integer form. For h=floor(t log₂(3/2)) and a=h+2, the block contracts exactly when u(2^{h+t+1}−3^t)>2^{h+1}−1. The open challenge is to control these u values across the coupled orbit.

notes.speaker: Codex · transition update
notes.text: At the sole possible mean-test gap, put M=2^{h+1} and D=2^{h+t+1}−3^t. If uD<M−1, the block expands but the exact transition gives a_next−1=v₂(Du+1)≤h, so the next high valuation is at least one smaller. Equality uD=M−1 returns to the same block start and is periodic. This does not settle the global orbit.

notes.speaker: Codex · transition refinement
notes.text: A strict expansion at the exceptional valuation has two exact next-block forms. With r=Du+1=2^b s and ℓ=t+h+1−b: s>1 forces a_next+t_next≤a_k−1; s=1 gives t_next=ℓ≥t+1 and preserves u_next=u. This narrows the local recurrence but leaves global orbit control open.

notes.speaker: Codex · next-block update
notes.text: The s=1 branch has a further consequence: b≤h≤t log₂(3/2), while t_next=ℓ≥t+1, so q_next=1+b/ℓ<log₂3. Hence the following block is forced to expand too. In the s>1 branch, t_next<t and a_next+t_next≤a_k−1. No global descent follows yet.

notes.speaker: Codex · potential update
notes.text: The finite-chain estimate sharpens using the strict decrease of t. For L consecutive exceptional-gap expansions starting at H_start, every link has s>1 and drops H by at least t+1; therefore (L+1)(L+2)≤2H_start and L≤floor((sqrt(8H_start+1)−3)/2).

notes.speaker: Codex · chain-growth update
notes.text: For a consecutive exceptional expansion chain, distinct t_i give total log₂ growth below Σ_{t≥1}β_t=−log₂P, where P=∏(1−2^{-t}). The elementary product bound P≥9/32 yields endpoint ratio (x_end+1)/(x_start+1)<32/9. Other block types remain uncontrolled.
